newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Utd News says no current HTV bid plans.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Utd News says no current HTV bid plans.

text.p: United News & Media Plc chief executive Clive Hollick said on Friday that the company had no current plans of bidding for ITV company HTV.
United News last year built up a 29.9 percent stake in HTV, the regional broadcaster to Wales and south-west England, but said at the time it was not planning a full bid.
"We haven't changed our view," Hollick told Reuters in a telephone interview. "We have a lot in common with HTV, which operates an adjacent franchise," he added.
United News has ITV franchises for southern and eastern England through its Meridian and Anglia units.
United News also has a stake of around 14 percent in Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Holdings Plc, the ITV company for large areas of northern England.
Shares in Yorkshire plunged on Thursday after Granada Group Plc, which controls some 27 percent of the company, said it had no current plans to make a bid.
Hollick described Yorkshire as a "successful company" and said United's investment had proved a sound one but would not comment further on the Yorkshire situation.
United's television interests also include a stake in Channel 5, the commercial station which launches on March 30.
"I think we are in for a pleasant surprise. I think it will do well," Hollick said, when asked how he viewed the launch.
United's 1996 accounts included 63 million pounds in start-up costs for Channel 5, which has employed thousands of retuners to adjust video recorders to prevent interference from its signal.
Profit before tax and exceptional items in 1996 rose 12 percent to 290.2 million pounds while earnings per share increased 15 percent to 40p.
"I think we have delivered at the top end of expectations against the agenda we set ourselves at the time of the merger," Hollick said.

United News owns national newspapers The Express and Daily Star. Hollick said savings at the newspapers would rise to around 15 million pounds annually and some of this would be reinvested in the titles.
